title: Seller's Property Condition Disclosure Statement
description: Kansas Statute §58-30,106 requires sellers of residential real property to provide a written disclosure statement to the buyer. The disclosure covers the condition of the property including structural, mechanical, environmental factors, and known defects. Kansas follows a modified caveat emptor approach where the statutory form creates the disclosure obligation. Certain transfers are exempt under K.S.A. §58-30,103.

required_actions.note: Must be provided before or at the time the buyer makes an offer. Exemptions for foreclosures, court orders, and transfers between co-owners.

title: Brokerage Relationship Disclosure
description: Kansas Statute §58-30,105 requires licensees to provide a written disclosure of brokerage relationships at the first substantial contact with a party. Kansas recognizes seller's agents, buyer's agents, dual agents (with written consent), and transaction brokers. The Kansas Real Estate Commission prescribes the disclosure form.

required_actions.note: Written disclosure at first substantial contact. Dual agency requires written informed consent from both parties. Transaction broker status is default if no other agreement.

title: Title Company or Escrow Closing
description: Kansas is a title company/escrow closing state. Closings are conducted by title companies or escrow agents. Attorney presence is not required by statute. Title insurance is standard practice for residential transactions. Kansas uses warranty deeds.

required_actions.note: Title companies typically handle closings. Attorney not required but recommended for complex transactions.

title: Real Estate Advertising Requirements
description: Kansas Administrative Regulation 86-3-17 and K.S.A. §58-3062 require that all real estate advertising include the licensed name of the supervising broker. Blind ads (without brokerage identification) are prohibited. Team names and branding must include or be accompanied by the brokerage name.

required_actions.note: All advertising must include the supervising broker's licensed name. Blind ads are prohibited. Internet advertising must comply with the same requirements.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978 Properties)
description: Federal law (42 U.S.C. §4852d) requires sellers of properties built before 1978 to disclose known lead-based paint hazards and provide EPA pamphlet. Kansas also enforces this through the Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE) lead program. Buyer receives 10-day inspection period.

required_actions.note: Buyer has 10-day right to conduct lead inspection (waivable). KDHE maintains additional lead-safe housing requirements.
